context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It strictly adheres to EU-only data residency constraints for GDPR compliance while maintaining high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- **Library Patrons (Members):** Access self-service portals to search catalogues and manage loans.
- **Librarians / Library Staff:** Utilize circulation and cataloguing tools (R-01) for inventory management.
- **Library Administrators:** Handle reporting and user management.
- **Inter-Library Loan (ILL) Partners:** External library systems for resource sharing.
- **Payment Gateways & Notification Services:** External SaaS for processing fines and alerts.
- **Library Management System (Core):** Central processing unit for core business logic.

## Relationships
- Patrons, Staff, and Admins interact via HTTPS with **TLS 1.3**.
- Core system integrates with ILL Partners via **NCIP/ISO 18626 APIs** using **mTLS**.
- External SaaS integrations communicate via secure webhooks protected by **mTLS**.

## Technology Stack
- **Search & Caching:** Elasticsearch or Redis to ensure 99th-percentile search response times under 800 ms (R-05).
- **Security & IAM:** OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (OIDC) with Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
- **Encryption:** AES-256 for data at rest.
- **Integration Patterns:** Asynchronous message queues and webhooks for ILL partners.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict compliance with EU-only data residency and GDPR mandates through isolated trust boundaries and encrypted data handling. Concurrently, it delivers high-performance search capabilities and fault-tolerant third-party integrations to support reliable library operations.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive platform for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It guarantees strict EU-only data residency while maintaining high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Members), Librarians, and Library Administrators
* Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal container
* API Gateway container
* Core Circulation and Transactional Database containers
* Read-optimized Search Index container (Elasticsearch)
* Admin/Reporting container
* Payment Gateway and Notification Service integration containers
* Inter-Library Loan (ILL) Partners external system

## Relationships
* Library Patrons and Staff interact with the Self-Service Portal and Admin containers via HTTPS (TLS 1.3).
* API Gateway routes traffic to backend containers using OAuth2/OIDC and enforces mTLS for container-to-container communication.
* Core containers query the EU-hosted Elasticsearch container for catalogue searches (R-01).
* External Payment Gateways and Notification Services integrate via egress boundary payload filtering.

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes: EU-region clusters for strict data residency enforcement.
* Elasticsearch: EU-hosted read-optimized search index for <800ms search SLA (R-05).
* ArgoCD: GitOps pipeline for immutable container deployments.
* OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing across API Gateway, Search, and Payment containers.
* TLS 1.3 & AES-256: Encryption standards for data in-transit and at rest.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the patron search and reporting workloads from the core transactional database to consistently achieve the required 99th-percentile search response under 800ms. Furthermore, it strictly enforces EU-only data residency and security compliance through localized infrastructure, mTLS, and egress PII payload filtering.

Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items and manage circulation. The Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal serves patrons and librarians with secure access, robust accessibility, and strict EU data residency.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Members)
* Librarians / Library Staff
* Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal (Web/Mobile)
* API Gateway (Kubernetes, OAuth2/OIDC, mTLS)
* Read-optimized Search Index (Elasticsearch, EU-hosted)
* External Services (Payment Gateways, Notification Services, ILL Partners)

## Relationships
* Library Patrons -> Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
* Librarians -> Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
* Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal -> API Gateway [HTTPS (TLS 1.3), OAuth2/OIDC, PKCE]
* API Gateway -> Read-optimized Search Index [gRPC/REST, mTLS]

## Technology Stack
* Frontend Assets: EU-hosted CDN with strict geo-pinning for EU data residency
* Authentication: OAuth2/OIDC with PKCE, HTTP-only Secure SameSite=Strict cookies
* Security: Subresource Integrity (SRI), Content Security Policy (CSP), platform-native secure enclaves (Keychain/Keystore)
* Observability: Real User Monitoring (RUM) for latency tracking (<800ms NFR)

## Rationale
The architecture ensures strict GDPR compliance and EU data residency via localized CDN deployment and zero-PII client caching. It guarantees high performance (<800ms search latency) through optimized search indexes and comprehensive RUM tracking.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for libraries while strictly enforcing EU data residency. The API Gateway secures, routes, and manages all ingress and egress traffic for the platform.

## Key Elements
* Users: Library Patrons, Librarians, Library Administrators
* External Systems: Inter-Library Loan (ILL) Partners, Payment Gateways & Notification Services
* Containers: Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal, API Gateway, Core Circulation and Transactional Database, Read-optimized Search Index, Admin/Reporting Container

## Relationships
* Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal -> API Gateway: Sends HTTPS (TLS 1.3), OAuth2/OIDC requests
* API Gateway -> Core Circulation and Transactional Database: Routes traffic via mTLS
* API Gateway -> Read-optimized Search Index: Routes search requests via mTLS
* API Gateway -> Admin/Reporting Container: Routes admin requests via mTLS
* API Gateway -> Payment Gateway and Notification Service: Integrates via HTTPS with Egress Filtering
* API Gateway -> Inter-Library Loan (ILL) Partners: Integrates via HTTPS with dynamic mTLS

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes: Container orchestration for scalable deployment of backend and gateway services
* OAuth2/OIDC & JWT: Edge token validation, scope enforcement, and role-based access control
* Elasticsearch: Read-optimized search index ensuring sub-800ms 99th-percentile response times
* cert-manager: Automated mTLS certificate issuance, rotation, and revocation

## Rationale
This architecture decouples edge security, routing, and operational controls from backend business logic to meet strict EU data compliance. The API Gateway ensures high performance, resilience, and security while protecting backend systems from abuse.

Core Circulation and Transactional Datab.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture ensures strict EU data residency and high performance for patrons and staff.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons (Members)
- Librarians / Library Staff
- Library Administrators
- Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal
- API Gateway
- Core Circulation and Transactional Database
- Read-optimized Search Index
- Admin/Reporting Container
- Inter-Library Loan (ILL) Partners
- Payment Gateways & Notification Services

## Relationships
- Self-Service Web/Mobile Portal -> API Gateway: Routes requests [HTTPS, OAuth2/OIDC]
- API Gateway -> Core Circulation and Transactional Database: Routes traffic and executes parameterized statements [mTLS]
- Core Circulation and Transactional Database -> Read-optimized Search Index: Queries search index [Internal Network]
- Core Circulation and Transactional Database -> Message Broker: Publishes domain events via Change Data Capture [Debezium, WAL, JWE]

## Technology Stack
- Kubernetes: Container orchestration for services with strict EU-region clustering
- PostgreSQL with Raft/Patroni: Core transactional database ensuring strong consistency and <200ms write-latency SLO
- Elasticsearch: Read-optimized search index for sub-800ms search response compliance
- HashiCorp Vault: Dynamic database credentials and secret rotation (max 24-hour TTL)
- Debezium: Change Data Capture (CDC) reading from database write-ahead log (WAL) for event-outbox pattern

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict EU data residency and robust security through zero-trust mTLS, AES-256 encryption, and JWE event payloads. It meets strict performance SLOs using Raft/Patroni synchronous replication and asynchronous event decoupling.

Read-optimized Search Index.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It utilizes a read-optimized search index to guarantee high-performance discovery.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons (Members) & Library Librarians / Staff
- API Gateway (Kubernetes, OAuth2/OIDC, mTLS)
- Read-optimized Search Index (Elasticsearch, EU-hosted)
- Core Circulation and Transactional Database (Kubernetes, EU-region clusters)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Read-optimized Search Index: Routes search requests with query-time JWT filtering [mTLS, TLS 1.3]
- Core Circulation Database -> Read-optimized Search Index: Streams updates via Change Data Capture pipeline [Debezium, TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- Elasticsearch: Read-optimized search engine chosen for sub-800ms performance and faceted search capabilities
- Debezium: Change Data Capture tool for near-real-time data synchronization preventing phantom availability
- Kubernetes: Container orchestration platform for resource isolation, operator management, and scaling
- Prometheus/Grafana: Observability stack for tracking JVM heap and query latency SLAs
- Vault / Kubernetes Secrets: Secret management for TLS certificates and keystore passwords

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict EU data residency compliance while meeting the stringent non-functional performance requirement of 99th-percentile search response under 800 ms. Security controls, CDC pipelines, and resource isolation ensure both data integrity and high availability during academic traffic surges.

  - type: "component"

    technology: "Debezium, Elasticsearch Sink"
    description: "Receives real-time database updates via Change Data Capture to maintain search index consistency."
relationships:
  - source: "Search Query Processor"
    destination: "Data Synchronization Consumer"
    description: "Accesses synchronized indices for discovery [TLS 1.3]"

Admin/Reporting Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides item cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for academic and public libraries. The Admin/Reporting Container handles administrative workloads, financial auditing, and data analytics while enforcing strict EU data residency.

## Key Elements
- Library Administrators, Financial Auditors, Library Data Analysts (Users)
- API Gateway (Kubernetes, OAuth2/OIDC, mTLS)
- Admin/Reporting Container (Kubernetes, EU-region)
- Core Circulation and Transactional Database (Kubernetes, EU-region clusters)
- Read-optimized Search Index (Elasticsearch, EU-hosted)

## Relationships
- Library Administrators -> Admin/Reporting Container [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- Financial Auditors / Data Analysts -> Admin/Reporting Container [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- API Gateway -> Admin/Reporting Container [mTLS]
- Admin/Reporting Container -> Core Circulation Database [Parameterized Queries, Read-Replicas]

## Technology Stack
- Kubernetes: Orchestrates containers with dedicated resource quotas and Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) for heavy reporting workloads.
- Prometheus: Tracks query execution times, export failure rates, and compliance metrics.
- Elasticsearch: Powers read-optimized search indices adhering to <800 ms performance goals.
- OAuth2/OIDC: Enforces Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and data minimization principles.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates resource-intensive reporting workloads using dedicated Kubernetes nodes and asynchronous workers, protecting core patron circulation performance. Strict EU data residency constraints and role-based data masking ensure compliance with privacy regulations.
